title: Sell Mineral Rights in Souris, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Souris, ND
metaDescription: Mineral rights near Souris, ND in the Mouse River valley? These Bottineau County interests deserve an honest look, not a guess. See what's involved.
heroLead: Souris sits along the Mouse River valley in Bottineau County, and the mineral interests tied to this stretch of the state usually trace back to river-bottom farmland that's been in one family for generations.
intro: Oil activity here has always been light compared to the Bakken counties, but Bottineau County has seen conventional wells come and go over the decades, and Souris-area tracts occasionally carry old lease history that families forget about until a statement or a notice shows up unexpectedly.

sections.heading: River valley ground, older lease patterns
paragraphs: Land along the Mouse River near Souris was often leased in blocks decades ago when conventional exploration moved through this part of the state, and some of those leases produced small amounts for years before quietly going dormant. If your family's paperwork references a lease from that era, we can check whether it's still active or has lapsed.

sections.heading: What we look at before making an offer
paragraphs: We pull the Bottineau County Recorder's records to confirm your legal description and ownership share, then check the state's well index for any historic or current activity nearby. Only after that do we tell you what we think a fair number looks like for your specific interest.

sections.heading: River-bottom farmland and how it's held today
paragraphs: Some of the strongest farm ground in Bottineau County sits along the Mouse River near Souris, and families who've worked that land for generations often kept the mineral rights separate even after selling or leasing the surface. If that's your situation, we treat the mineral interest as its own asset, distinct from whatever happened to the farmland itself.
We'll research your legal description independently, so the sale reflects only the minerals you actually hold.

faqs.question: Our family lease near Souris is decades old. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can. Some older leases lapsed without formal release, which affects how we handle the sale. We check the current status before making an offer.

faqs.question: How do you determine value for an interest with no recent royalty checks?
faqs.answer: We look at historical production, nearby activity, and the county's broader well record rather than relying only on recent statements, since Souris-area interests often have gaps in production history.

faqs.question: Can we sell just part of the mineral interest and keep the rest?
faqs.answer: In most cases yes. Partial sales are common, and we can structure an offer for a portion of your interest if that fits your family's situation better than selling everything.

faqs.question: We sold the farmland years ago but think we kept the minerals. How do we confirm that?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever paperwork you have from the sale, and we'll check the Bottineau County Recorder's file to confirm whether the mineral rights were reserved.
